ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of a semicircle, and $C$, $D$ are two points on the semicircle. Given that $ \angle ADC=105^\circ$, what is the measure of $ \angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $A,B,C,D$ are points on the circle $\odot O$ and $\angle ADC=105^\circ$,

it follows that $\angle ABC=180^\circ-105^\circ=\boxed{75^\circ}$

method.method_draft: First read the figure as points A, D, C, B lying on one circle, with D and C on the upper semicircular arc between A and B. From the text, ∠ADC = 105°. Use the inscribed-angle theorem: ∠ADC intercepts the arc AC that does not contain D. Since its measure is 105°, that intercepted arc has measure 2×105° = 210°. The full circle is 360°, so the other arc AC, the one not containing B and seen by ∠ABC, has measure 360° - 210° = 150°. Again by the inscribed-angle theorem, ∠ABC equals half of that arc, so ∠ABC = 150°/2 = 75°.
